description: Quaker Chemical Corporation, doing business as Quaker Houghton, provides industrial process fluids worldwide. The company develops, produces, and markets various formulated specialty chemical products
description_full: Quaker Chemical Corporation, doing business as Quaker Houghton, provides industrial process fluids worldwide. The company develops, produces, and markets various formulated specialty chemical products; and offers chemical management services for various heavy industrial and manufacturing applications. It offers metal removal fluids, cleaning fluids, corrosion inhibitors, metal drawing and forming fluids, die cast mold releases, heat treatment and quenchants, metal forging and hydraulic fluids, specialty greases, offshore sub-sea energy control fluids, rolling lubricants, and rod and wire drawing fluids. The company serves steel, aluminum, automotive, aerospace, offshore, container, mining, and metalworking companies. Quaker Chemical Corporation was founded in 1918 and is headquartered in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania.

financial_summary: Quaker Houghton is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $2.6B market cap on $1.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -1% over the past three years and +10% annually across the full decade — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.
Returns on capital run at 6% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 36%.
The business throws off $81M in free cash flow — roughly 4 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 5.8× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 1.2× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 2.9% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 22% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.2× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
